text.p: Tower Air said Monday that an upturn in business during 1997 and its cost-reduction program "will have their effect by mid-year, paving the way for a profitable 1997."
The company reported 1996 revenues of $417.8 million versus $490.5 million in 1995 and a net loss of $20.9 million or $1.37 per share versus a profit of $10.7 million or $0.70 per share in 1995.

The company attributed its 1996 losses to a decline in travel to Israel, one of its major markets. And Tower said concern over safety resulting from air crashes over the last 18 months contributed to a decline in domestic passengers.
Tower said it expects more revenue from Israeli routes as travel increases in an improving tourist market.
